purpose: What a document says about academic misconduct involving AI: what counts as an offence, how it is detected, how a case is handled, and what the outcomes are. Each value has a verbatim quote and a flag for whether the quote itself names AI. Rules about what AI may be used for are in the uses schema, not here.

offences.undeclared_use: using AI without the required acknowledgement or declaration
offences.unauthorised_use: using AI beyond what the module, brief or institution permits
offences.passing_off: presenting AI-generated work as one's own, false authorship, or plagiarism of AI output
offences.fabrication_or_falsification: fabricating or falsifying data, references, quotations or results (with or without AI)
offences.disguising_use: hiding AI use or evading detection (humanising or paraphrasing tools, editing to avoid detectors)
offences.contract_cheating_or_ghostwriting: having a third party, essay mill or AI produce work on the student's behalf
offences.misuse_of_others_work: copying, paraphrasing or submitting other people's work, including other students' work
offences.exam_or_supervised_breach: using AI in an exam or supervised assessment where not permitted
offences.data_or_upload_breach: uploading personal, confidential, copyright or university material to AI tools against the rules
offences.facilitating_or_collusion: helping, enabling or colluding with another person's misconduct (aiding, abetting, sharing work)
offences.impersonation_or_coercion: impersonation, bribery, coercion or other deception of staff or fellow students
offences.self_plagiarism_or_multiple_submission: reusing one's own earlier work or submitting the same work more than once

liability.strict_liability: ignorance, accident or lack of intent is no defence
liability.intent_considered: intent, carelessness or awareness affects the outcome
liability.ignorance_mitigates: inexperience or ignorance can count in the student's favour

methods.ai_detection_software: software that estimates whether text is AI-generated
methods.staff_judgement: marker or staff judgement of style, content or quality
methods.oral_viva_or_interview: a viva, interview or oral check of understanding
methods.draft_or_version_history: drafts, notes, version history or logs as evidence
methods.forensic_or_specialist_analysis: referral for specialist or digital forensic analysis

stances.used: the document says the method is used
stances.may_be_used: the document says the method may be used or that use may be detected
stances.not_used: the document says the method is not used
stances.restricted: use is limited to named officers or conditions
stances.unreliable: the document warns the method is unreliable or not enough on its own

process.informal_conversation: an informal discussion or conversation first
process.referral_to_officer_or_panel: referral to an officer, committee or panel
process.student_right_to_respond: the student is told the allegation and may respond
process.proceeds_if_absent: the case proceeds if the student does not attend or respond
process.support_for_student: support or representation is offered (students' union, adviser)
process.timescale: a stated timescale for the process
process.standard_of_proof: a stated standard of proof (for example balance of probabilities)
process.records_or_register: a record or register of cases is kept

outcomes.educative_first_offence: a first or minor offence is handled educatively
outcomes.zero_for_work: a mark of zero for the work
outcomes.degree_effect: an effect on the degree classification or award
outcomes.repeat_offence_escalation: repeat or concurrent offences are treated more severely
outcomes.tariff_or_factors: a penalty tariff or stated factors that set the penalty
outcomes.penalty_stated_without_detail: penalties are mentioned but not specified
outcomes.mark_cap: a cap on the mark (for example resubmission capped at the pass mark)
outcomes.award_withdrawn_or_post_award: withdrawal of an award or a procedure for cases found after the award
outcomes.professional_referral: referral to a professional or fitness-to-practise body

definitions: terms defined by the document (contract cheating, false authorship, plagiarism, collusion), free text of at most four words

scope.ai_specific: the document is mainly about AI
scope.general_misconduct: the document is a general misconduct procedure with some AI wording
scope.none: the document has no misconduct content
